summary: @lyxa.ai/core auto-connects on import to author-controlled AMQP broker and executes remote-supplied method dispatch
details: On require of @lyxa.ai/core, dist/index.js unconditionally invokes bootstrapCore() at module top level, which calls initEventBus("amqps://vgyuplrd:<embedded-credentials>@dog.lmq.cloudamqp.com/vgyuplrd") and opens an authenticated AMQP connection to a hardcoded CloudAMQP broker at dog.lmq.cloudamqp.com. The consumer registers channel.consume handlers that JSON.parse incoming messages and invoke instance[methodName](payload) on registered service singletons inside the importing process, giving the operator of the broker a remote-triggered code-execution channel into any process that imports the package. dist/libraries/secrets/index.js also embeds a full Google Cloud service account credential (client_email lyxa-core@for-poc-325210.iam.gserviceaccount.com, project for-poc-325210, full private_key PEM) and uses it to instantiate SecretManagerServiceClient, which on import fetches secrets such as MONGO_URL from the author's GCP project (projects/899369746265) and then connects the installer's process to the author-owned MongoDB. The package's main entry runs bootstrapCore with environment DEV and instanceType "attemptedStartup", consistent with an internal service accidentally published to the public npm registry with production credentials embedded; the installer-side effect — silent auto-attachment to author-controlled AMQP and MongoDB plus a remote-driven method-dispatch channel — is present regardless of intent.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
